rv.q: It is delightful to be able to say that right here is a landmark theatrical production that will be talked about for years to come.
Imelda Staunton plays Dolly to perfection.
Dominic Cooke’s production is immaculately performed and slowly, beautifully life-affirming, with humour that reins in the schmaltz.
In this joyful, sensitive interpretation they prove the enduring chemistry of their creative partnership.
Cooke's production – five years, one pandemic and a venue-change in the making – is worth the wait.
It’s an irresistible performance.
She takes infectious, childlike pleasure in her role and ensures this very jolly, Dolly mixture is well worth a guzzle.
This Dolly is a complete delight.
Anyone craving a taste of good old-fashioned razzmatazz won’t be disappointed in Hello, Dolly!, a 1964 musical served up with all the trimmings in the Palladium’s vast gilded barn.
This is a terrific old-fashioned show which audiences love, and it knows it.
Staunton smashes it with sincerity and sass.
The star raises the roof without breaking into a sweat
This giddily magnificent, life-affirming production will certainly spread joy.
This is a big, spectacular show that carries you away to a bygone era.
Refunds are in order if you don't feel you've got your money's worth from the title number alone, and you don't get a high from it; no takers expected...
It’s simply a marvellous show with some outstanding songs and large set piece moments...
The production’s knockabout energy sends the soul soaring.
Cooke and company have seized an old-fashioned show, unexpectedly provided vanishingly rare but hugely welcome genuine charm, and made it zing.
For all those who love this great Broadway musical, the present revival is not to be missed.
This is giddy, Golden-age glitz.

Musical direction is under the control of Nicholas Slilbeck who uses his near full-sized orchestra to create a lush and luxurious sound which fills the auditorium and the hearts of the entire audience.
Staunton’s Dolly is a force of nature, running rings around Andy Nyman’s blustering Horace to deliver the star turn that keeps this show on the road.
This is one case where every element came together beautifully to create pure theatre magic and the result is one of the best shows of the year.
This terrific Hello, Dolly! is a reminder of the power of musical theatre to lift spirits and touch hearts.

There is no denying the powerhouse performance of Imelda Staunton who embraces the role with characteristic energy and intelligence, bringing light and shade to Dolly that only a serious actor at the top of her game could achieve.

It’s best when it bolts along and veers away from sentimentality, and Staunton gets this: she always has a glint in her eye that shows she’s in on the joke. Oh, and she can sing! She belts the titular track in act two in a way that makes you feel perplexed as to why she hasn’t done much more of this...

cn.t: Imelda Staunton triumphs in this lavish, long-delayed West End revival, delivering a powerhouse performance that brings heart and emotional depth to Jerry Herman's classic. Critics hail the production as a dazzling spectacle and the musical event of the summer.
